# Server reference

<!-- Generated by scripts/gen-reference.sh from `grovedockd --version`: grovedockd 4.0.0. Do not edit by hand. -->

Every `grovedockd` command and option, as printed by `--help`. Options listed under `grovedockd` itself apply to every command and go before it (`grovedockd --metrics 0.0.0.0:9420 server ...`). Each option's environment variable is shown in brackets. The most used settings are summarised in [Configuration](configuration.md).

## `grovedockd`

```text
Grovedock: source control server, regional cache and node daemon

Usage: grovedockd [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  server   Authoritative server: all features, durable storage
  license  Support licences: `grovedockd license verify FILE`
  repo     Operator actions on one hosted repository, straight on the registry (site administration; works while the server runs, which notices within seconds)
  token    Create an access token directly in a platform registry, without a running server: how the first administrator gets in. Prints the token once
  backup   Back up a platform server while it runs: a consistent snapshot of the registry and of every hosted repository's metadata database, with a manifest of where each belongs and where objects live. Restore by copying back while stopped (docs/backup.md)
  compact  Delta-compress stored blob versions (single writer; safe to run while serving)
  copy     Copy a repository to another store: a backup, a restore, or a move to another backend (e.g. SQLite to Postgres). Safe while the source serves; repeat it to copy only what is new
  cache    Regional cache: stateless, memory-bounded, read-through to an upstream tier
  daemon   Per-node daemon: memory + local disk cache shared by every job on the machine
  help     Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
      --metrics <METRICS>
          Address for `/metrics` (Prometheus), `/healthz` and `/readyz` (no token needed), e.g. 0.0.0.0:9420 [env: GD_METRICS=]
      --log-json
          Emit JSON logs [env: GD_LOG_JSON=]
      --audit-log <AUDIT_LOG>
          Append an audit trail (JSON lines: who read or changed what, from where, with what result) to this file. Off by default; it grows with every request [env: GD_AUDIT_LOG=]
      --audit-retention-days <AUDIT_RETENTION_DAYS>
          Days of audit files to keep (one file per UTC day); 0 keeps all. 365 suits hosted services (docs/deploy.md) [env: GD_AUDIT_RETENTION_DAYS=] [default: 365]
      --cors-origin <WEB_ORIGINS>
          Origins allowed to call this server from a browser on another site (repeatable or comma-separated), e.g. your own console's address. Default: none (same origin only); `*` allows any (development only) [env: GD_WEB_ORIGINS=] [alias: --web-origins]
      --trust-proxy
          Take the client address (audit log, sign-in rate limits) from `X-Forwarded-For` when the connection comes from a reverse proxy on this host (loopback) [env: GD_TRUST_PROXY=]
      --max-request-mb <MAX_REQUEST_MB>
          Largest request message in MiB (an uploaded object batch, a changeset). Default: 64 with --platform, 260 otherwise. Files of 8 MiB and more are uploaded in chunks [env: GD_MAX_REQUEST_MB=]
      --max-calls-per-principal <MAX_CALLS_PER_PRINCIPAL>
          Calls one account may have in progress at once (0: no limit). Default: 128 with --platform, no limit otherwise [env: GD_MAX_CALLS_PER_PRINCIPAL=]
      --sqlite-synchronous <SQLITE_SYNCHRONOUS>
          SQLite durability: `full` (default) syncs every commit, so an acknowledged land survives power loss; `normal` survives process crashes only, for more throughput on a slow disk [env: GD_SQLITE_SYNCHRONOUS=] [default: full] [possible values: full, normal]
      --allow-anonymous
          Accept unauthenticated calls on a non-loopback address. Without tokens or OIDC, grovedockd otherwise listens only on localhost, so a server is never open to a network by accident [env: GD_ALLOW_ANONYMOUS=]
      --request-timeout <REQUEST_TIMEOUT>
          Longest any one call may run, in seconds [env: GD_REQUEST_TIMEOUT=] [default: 600]
      --max-in-flight <MAX_IN_FLIGHT>
          Calls in progress at once across all clients; beyond this, calls are refused with Unavailable (clients retry) instead of queueing [env: GD_MAX_IN_FLIGHT=] [default: 4096]
      --tokens <TOKENS>
          Comma-separated bearer tokens accepted by this process. Unset = no auth (dev only) [env: GD_TOKENS]
      --oidc-issuer <OIDC_ISSUER>
          OpenID Connect issuer URL; enables SSO bearer tokens (JWTs) alongside static tokens [env: GD_OIDC_ISSUER=]
      --oidc-audience <OIDC_AUDIENCE>
          Expected `aud` claim of OIDC tokens [env: GD_OIDC_AUDIENCE=]
      --oidc-claim <OIDC_CLAIM>
          Claim used as the principal for access rules (sub, email, preferred_username...) [env: GD_OIDC_CLAIM=] [default: sub]
      --oidc-require <OIDC_REQUIRE>
          CLAIM=VALUE every OIDC token must carry (repeatable; all must match), e.g. `repository_owner=acme`, `hd=corp.example`, `email_verified=true`. Required for issuers that serve anyone (GitHub Actions, Google) [env: GD_OIDC_REQUIRE=]
      --oidc-admin <OIDC_ADMINS>
          Platform administrators who may sign in through OIDC (repeatable). Any other `--platform-admins` login is refused from an OIDC token, so an identity provider that lets users pick their name can't make someone an administrator [env: GD_OIDC_ADMINS=]
      --tls-cert <TLS_CERT>
          PEM certificate and key for TLS [env: GD_TLS_CERT=]
      --tls-key <TLS_KEY>
          [env: GD_TLS_KEY=]
  -h, --help
          Print help
  -V, --version
          Print version
```

## `grovedockd server`

```text
Authoritative server: all features, durable storage

Usage: grovedockd server [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --listen <LISTEN>
          [default: 127.0.0.1:7420]

      --metadata <METADATA>
          memory | sqlite://PATH | postgres://... Default: sqlite://./gd-data/meta.db, or memory with --platform (whose clients can't reach this repository)

          [env: GD_METADATA]

      --objects <OBJECTS>
          metadata | file:///PATH | s3://BUCKET/PREFIX | gs://BUCKET | az://CONTAINER | memory:///

          [env: GD_OBJECTS]
          [default: metadata]

      --acl <ACL>
          JSON access rules (per-directory write and per-ref permissions). Unset = allow all

          [env: GD_ACL=]

      --land-hook <LAND_HOOK>
          Pre-land check: every land is POSTed here and proceeds only on a 2xx answer

          [env: GD_LAND_HOOK]

      --land-hook-token <LAND_HOOK_TOKEN>
          Bearer token sent to the land hook

          [env: GD_LAND_HOOK_TOKEN]

      --land-hook-timeout <LAND_HOOK_TIMEOUT>
          Seconds to wait for the land hook before refusing the land

          [default: 10]

      --platform <PLATFORM>
          Host many repositories: the registry of which exist (sqlite://PATH or memory). Without it the server hosts one repository, `--metadata` / `--objects`

          [env: GD_PLATFORM]

      --repos-metadata <REPOS_METADATA>
          Storage for each hosted repository; `{repo}` becomes OWNER/NAME and `{repo_id}` OWNER--NAME, e.g. sqlite:///var/lib/gd/repos/{repo}.db

          [env: GD_REPOS_METADATA]

      --metrics <METRICS>
          Address for `/metrics` (Prometheus), `/healthz` and `/readyz` (no token needed), e.g. 0.0.0.0:9420

          [env: GD_METRICS=]

      --repos-objects <REPOS_OBJECTS>
          Objects for each hosted repository (same placeholders), or `metadata`

          [env: GD_REPOS_OBJECTS]
          [default: metadata]

      --log-json
          Emit JSON logs

          [env: GD_LOG_JSON=]

      --platform-admins <PLATFORM_ADMINS>
          Logins that administer the whole server: create organisations, and act as an administrator of every organisation and repository

          [env: GD_PLATFORM_ADMINS=]

      --audit-log <AUDIT_LOG>
          Append an audit trail (JSON lines: who read or changed what, from where, with what result) to this file. Off by default; it grows with every request

          [env: GD_AUDIT_LOG=]

      --multi-tenant
          Strangers share this server (a hosted service): internal repositories are for the owning organisation only, organisations add existing accounts only, and any person may create a few organisations

          [env: GD_MULTI_TENANT=]

      --audit-retention-days <AUDIT_RETENTION_DAYS>
          Days of audit files to keep (one file per UTC day); 0 keeps all. 365 suits hosted services (docs/deploy.md)

          [env: GD_AUDIT_RETENTION_DAYS=]
          [default: 365]

      --max-orgs-per-account <MAX_ORGS_PER_ACCOUNT>
          With --multi-tenant: how many organisations a person may administer

          [env: GD_MAX_ORGS_PER_ACCOUNT=]
          [default: 3]

      --cors-origin <WEB_ORIGINS>
          Origins allowed to call this server from a browser on another site (repeatable or comma-separated), e.g. your own console's address. Default: none (same origin only); `*` allows any (development only)

          [env: GD_WEB_ORIGINS=]
          [alias: --web-origins]

      --webhook-allow-private
          Let webhooks call loopback and private networks (self-hosted CI on an internal network). Cloud metadata addresses stay refused

          [env: GD_WEBHOOK_ALLOW_PRIVATE=]

      --login-listen <LOGIN_LISTEN>
          Serve the sign-in pages (`/login/*`: OpenID Connect providers such as Google, and email links) on this address, behind the same host name as the console

          [env: GD_LOGIN_LISTEN=]

      --trust-proxy
          Take the client address (audit log, sign-in rate limits) from `X-Forwarded-For` when the connection comes from a reverse proxy on this host (loopback)

          [env: GD_TRUST_PROXY=]

      --max-request-mb <MAX_REQUEST_MB>
          Largest request message in MiB (an uploaded object batch, a changeset). Default: 64 with --platform, 260 otherwise. Files of 8 MiB and more are uploaded in chunks

          [env: GD_MAX_REQUEST_MB=]

      --public-url <PUBLIC_URL>
          Where people reach this server, e.g. https://gd.example.com: the base of sign-in redirect addresses and email links

          [env: GD_PUBLIC_URL=]

      --max-calls-per-principal <MAX_CALLS_PER_PRINCIPAL>
          Calls one account may have in progress at once (0: no limit). Default: 128 with --platform, no limit otherwise

          [env: GD_MAX_CALLS_PER_PRINCIPAL=]

      --oidc <ID=ISSUER_URL>
          A sign-in provider, ID=ISSUER_URL (repeatable), e.g. google=https://accounts.google.com. Its client comes from GD_OIDC_<ID>_CLIENT_ID and GD_OIDC_<ID>_CLIENT_SECRET (or _FILE variants). GitHub isn't one: it signs in with GD_GITHUB_CLIENT_ID and GD_GITHUB_CLIENT_SECRET

          [env: GD_OIDC=]

      --smtp-url <SMTP_URL>
          Mail server for sign-in links: smtps://HOST:465 or smtp://HOST:587?tls=required. Credentials from GD_SMTP_USERNAME and GD_SMTP_PASSWORD (or _FILE variants)

          [env: GD_SMTP_URL]

      --sqlite-synchronous <SQLITE_SYNCHRONOUS>
          SQLite durability: `full` (default) syncs every commit, so an acknowledged land survives power loss; `normal` survives process crashes only, for more throughput on a slow disk

          [env: GD_SQLITE_SYNCHRONOUS=]
          [default: full]
          [possible values: full, normal]

      --allow-anonymous
          Accept unauthenticated calls on a non-loopback address. Without tokens or OIDC, grovedockd otherwise listens only on localhost, so a server is never open to a network by accident

          [env: GD_ALLOW_ANONYMOUS=]

      --mail-from <MAIL_FROM>
          Sender of sign-in links, e.g. "Grovedock <login@example.com>"

          [env: GD_MAIL_FROM=]

      --request-timeout <REQUEST_TIMEOUT>
          Longest any one call may run, in seconds

          [env: GD_REQUEST_TIMEOUT=]
          [default: 600]

      --turnstile-site-key <TURNSTILE_SITE_KEY>
          Cloudflare Turnstile site key for the email form; its secret comes from GD_TURNSTILE_SECRET (or _FILE). Unset: no challenge

          [env: GD_TURNSTILE_SITE_KEY=]

      --max-in-flight <MAX_IN_FLIGHT>
          Calls in progress at once across all clients; beyond this, calls are refused with Unavailable (clients retry) instead of queueing

          [env: GD_MAX_IN_FLIGHT=]
          [default: 4096]

      --signup <SIGNUP>
          Who may create an account by signing in: open (anyone; plans and limits keep free accounts in bounds) or closed (invitations only). Existing accounts can always sign in

          Possible values:
          - open:   Anyone who signs in gets an account (plans and limits keep a free account in bounds)
          - closed: No new accounts

          [env: GD_SIGNUP=]
          [default: open]

      --terms-url <TERMS_URL>
          Your terms of service, linked from the box people tick (18 or older, accept the terms) before an account is made

          [env: GD_TERMS_URL=]

      --tokens <TOKENS>
          Comma-separated bearer tokens accepted by this process. Unset = no auth (dev only)

          [env: GD_TOKENS]

      --oidc-issuer <OIDC_ISSUER>
          OpenID Connect issuer URL; enables SSO bearer tokens (JWTs) alongside static tokens

          [env: GD_OIDC_ISSUER=]

      --privacy-url <PRIVACY_URL>
          Your privacy policy, linked next to the terms

          [env: GD_PRIVACY_URL=]

      --max-open-repos <MAX_OPEN_REPOS>
          Most hosted repositories open at once; the least recently used idle ones close

          [env: GD_MAX_OPEN_REPOS=]
          [default: 256]

      --oidc-audience <OIDC_AUDIENCE>
          Expected `aud` claim of OIDC tokens

          [env: GD_OIDC_AUDIENCE=]

      --oidc-claim <OIDC_CLAIM>
          Claim used as the principal for access rules (sub, email, preferred_username...)

          [env: GD_OIDC_CLAIM=]
          [default: sub]

      --repo-idle-minutes <REPO_IDLE_MINUTES>
          Minutes an unused hosted repository stays open

          [env: GD_REPO_IDLE_MINUTES=]
          [default: 10]

      --default-org-limits <DEFAULT_ORG_LIMITS>
          With --multi-tenant: limits of organisations that have none of their own, e.g. `seats=5,agents=20,storage=1GiB,private_repos=unlimited,plan=Free` (ADR-035). Without it, organisations are unlimited until given limits (`gd admin limits set`)

          [env: GD_DEFAULT_ORG_LIMITS=]

      --oidc-require <OIDC_REQUIRE>
          CLAIM=VALUE every OIDC token must carry (repeatable; all must match), e.g. `repository_owner=acme`, `hd=corp.example`, `email_verified=true`. Required for issuers that serve anyone (GitHub Actions, Google)

          [env: GD_OIDC_REQUIRE=]

      --default-personal-limits <DEFAULT_PERSONAL_LIMITS>
          With --multi-tenant: limits of people's own accounts (repositories under their own login), e.g. `agents=2,storage=1GiB,private_repos=3,plan=Personal`. Without it, personal accounts are unlimited

          [env: GD_DEFAULT_PERSONAL_LIMITS=]

      --oidc-admin <OIDC_ADMINS>
          Platform administrators who may sign in through OIDC (repeatable). Any other `--platform-admins` login is refused from an OIDC token, so an identity provider that lets users pick their name can't make someone an administrator

          [env: GD_OIDC_ADMINS=]

      --billing-url <BILLING_URL>
          Where organisation administrators change their plan; the console's Upgrade button and limit messages link here

          [env: GD_BILLING_URL=]
          [default: ""]

      --tls-cert <TLS_CERT>
          PEM certificate and key for TLS

          [env: GD_TLS_CERT=]

      --support-url <SUPPORT_URL>
          Where people reach support, e.g. a suspended organisation (mailto: or https:); the console links to it

          [env: GD_SUPPORT_URL=]
          [default: ""]

      --tls-key <TLS_KEY>
          [env: GD_TLS_KEY=]

      --license <LICENSE>
          A support licence file to check at startup. Nothing is turned off without one

          [env: GD_LICENSE=]

      --console-dir <CONSOLE_DIR>
          Serve the web console from this directory (the release's `gd-console-VERSION` archive, unpacked) at `/` on the server's own address. Needs the `web` flag

          [env: GD_CONSOLE_DIR=]

      --git-dir <GIT_DIR>
          Serve git's own HTTP protocol (`git clone https://HOST/OWNER/NAME.git`), keeping a git mirror of each repository in this directory. Needs `git` and `git-remote-gd` (next to grovedockd) on the server, and --platform

          [env: GD_GIT_DIR=]

      --git-self-url <GIT_SELF_URL>
          How the git mirrors reach this server's gRPC (default: http://127.0.0.1:PORT of --listen)

          [env: GD_GIT_SELF_URL=]

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
```

## `grovedockd repo`

```text
Operator actions on one hosted repository, straight on the registry (site administration; works while the server runs, which notices within seconds)

Usage: grovedockd repo [OPTIONS] --platform <PLATFORM> <COMMAND>

Commands:
  disable  Take a repository down at once: every read and write is refused ("disabled by the operator"); nothing is deleted. Undo with `enable`
  enable   Serve a disabled repository again
  deleted  Repositories deleted from the web app or API and kept, hidden, until purged: their hidden names and when they were deleted
  restore  Bring back a deleted repository under its old name (or `--as` another)
  delete   Delete a repository for good: its registry rows (reviews, issues, webhooks, grants) and its storage files. Also purges one deleted from the web app (by its hidden name). Cannot be undone; take a backup first
  help     Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
      --platform <PLATFORM>
          [env: GD_PLATFORM]
      --metrics <METRICS>
          Address for `/metrics` (Prometheus), `/healthz` and `/readyz` (no token needed), e.g. 0.0.0.0:9420 [env: GD_METRICS=]
      --log-json
          Emit JSON logs [env: GD_LOG_JSON=]
      --audit-log <AUDIT_LOG>
          Append an audit trail (JSON lines: who read or changed what, from where, with what result) to this file. Off by default; it grows with every request [env: GD_AUDIT_LOG=]
      --audit-retention-days <AUDIT_RETENTION_DAYS>
          Days of audit files to keep (one file per UTC day); 0 keeps all. 365 suits hosted services (docs/deploy.md) [env: GD_AUDIT_RETENTION_DAYS=] [default: 365]
      --cors-origin <WEB_ORIGINS>
          Origins allowed to call this server from a browser on another site (repeatable or comma-separated), e.g. your own console's address. Default: none (same origin only); `*` allows any (development only) [env: GD_WEB_ORIGINS=] [alias: --web-origins]
      --trust-proxy
          Take the client address (audit log, sign-in rate limits) from `X-Forwarded-For` when the connection comes from a reverse proxy on this host (loopback) [env: GD_TRUST_PROXY=]
      --max-request-mb <MAX_REQUEST_MB>
          Largest request message in MiB (an uploaded object batch, a changeset). Default: 64 with --platform, 260 otherwise. Files of 8 MiB and more are uploaded in chunks [env: GD_MAX_REQUEST_MB=]
      --max-calls-per-principal <MAX_CALLS_PER_PRINCIPAL>
          Calls one account may have in progress at once (0: no limit). Default: 128 with --platform, no limit otherwise [env: GD_MAX_CALLS_PER_PRINCIPAL=]
      --sqlite-synchronous <SQLITE_SYNCHRONOUS>
          SQLite durability: `full` (default) syncs every commit, so an acknowledged land survives power loss; `normal` survives process crashes only, for more throughput on a slow disk [env: GD_SQLITE_SYNCHRONOUS=] [default: full] [possible values: full, normal]
      --allow-anonymous
          Accept unauthenticated calls on a non-loopback address. Without tokens or OIDC, grovedockd otherwise listens only on localhost, so a server is never open to a network by accident [env: GD_ALLOW_ANONYMOUS=]
      --request-timeout <REQUEST_TIMEOUT>
          Longest any one call may run, in seconds [env: GD_REQUEST_TIMEOUT=] [default: 600]
      --max-in-flight <MAX_IN_FLIGHT>
          Calls in progress at once across all clients; beyond this, calls are refused with Unavailable (clients retry) instead of queueing [env: GD_MAX_IN_FLIGHT=] [default: 4096]
      --tokens <TOKENS>
          Comma-separated bearer tokens accepted by this process. Unset = no auth (dev only) [env: GD_TOKENS]
      --oidc-issuer <OIDC_ISSUER>
          OpenID Connect issuer URL; enables SSO bearer tokens (JWTs) alongside static tokens [env: GD_OIDC_ISSUER=]
      --oidc-audience <OIDC_AUDIENCE>
          Expected `aud` claim of OIDC tokens [env: GD_OIDC_AUDIENCE=]
      --oidc-claim <OIDC_CLAIM>
          Claim used as the principal for access rules (sub, email, preferred_username...) [env: GD_OIDC_CLAIM=] [default: sub]
      --oidc-require <OIDC_REQUIRE>
          CLAIM=VALUE every OIDC token must carry (repeatable; all must match), e.g. `repository_owner=acme`, `hd=corp.example`, `email_verified=true`. Required for issuers that serve anyone (GitHub Actions, Google) [env: GD_OIDC_REQUIRE=]
      --oidc-admin <OIDC_ADMINS>
          Platform administrators who may sign in through OIDC (repeatable). Any other `--platform-admins` login is refused from an OIDC token, so an identity provider that lets users pick their name can't make someone an administrator [env: GD_OIDC_ADMINS=]
      --tls-cert <TLS_CERT>
          PEM certificate and key for TLS [env: GD_TLS_CERT=]
      --tls-key <TLS_KEY>
          [env: GD_TLS_KEY=]
  -h, --help
          Print help
```

```text

          [env: GD_PLATFORM]
      --account <ACCOUNT>
          The account the token belongs to and acts as (list it in --platform-admins to make it an administrator)

          [default: bootstrap]
      --expires-days <EXPIRES_DAYS>
          Days until it expires (1–366) [default: 30]
      --metrics <METRICS>
          Address for `/metrics` (Prometheus), `/healthz` and `/readyz` (no token needed), e.g. 0.0.0.0:9420 [env: GD_METRICS=]
      --log-json
          Emit JSON logs [env: GD_LOG_JSON=]
      --audit-log <AUDIT_LOG>
          Append an audit trail (JSON lines: who read or changed what, from where, with what result) to this file. Off by default; it grows with every request [env: GD_AUDIT_LOG=]
      --audit-retention-days <AUDIT_RETENTION_DAYS>
          Days of audit files to keep (one file per UTC day); 0 keeps all. 365 suits hosted services (docs/deploy.md) [env: GD_AUDIT_RETENTION_DAYS=] [default: 365]
      --cors-origin <WEB_ORIGINS>
          Origins allowed to call this server from a browser on another site (repeatable or comma-separated), e.g. your own console's address. Default: none (same origin only); `*` allows any (development only) [env: GD_WEB_ORIGINS=] [alias: --web-origins]
      --trust-proxy
          Take the client address (audit log, sign-in rate limits) from `X-Forwarded-For` when the connection comes from a reverse proxy on this host (loopback) [env: GD_TRUST_PROXY=]
      --max-request-mb <MAX_REQUEST_MB>
          Largest request message in MiB (an uploaded object batch, a changeset). Default: 64 with --platform, 260 otherwise. Files of 8 MiB and more are uploaded in chunks [env: GD_MAX_REQUEST_MB=]
      --max-calls-per-principal <MAX_CALLS_PER_PRINCIPAL>
          Calls one account may have in progress at once (0: no limit). Default: 128 with --platform, no limit otherwise [env: GD_MAX_CALLS_PER_PRINCIPAL=]
      --sqlite-synchronous <SQLITE_SYNCHRONOUS>
          SQLite durability: `full` (default) syncs every commit, so an acknowledged land survives power loss; `normal` survives process crashes only, for more throughput on a slow disk [env: GD_SQLITE_SYNCHRONOUS=] [default: full] [possible values: full, normal]
      --allow-anonymous
          Accept unauthenticated calls on a non-loopback address. Without tokens or OIDC, grovedockd otherwise listens only on localhost, so a server is never open to a network by accident [env: GD_ALLOW_ANONYMOUS=]
      --request-timeout <REQUEST_TIMEOUT>
          Longest any one call may run, in seconds [env: GD_REQUEST_TIMEOUT=] [default: 600]
      --max-in-flight <MAX_IN_FLIGHT>
          Calls in progress at once across all clients; beyond this, calls are refused with Unavailable (clients retry) instead of queueing [env: GD_MAX_IN_FLIGHT=] [default: 4096]
      --tokens <TOKENS>
          Comma-separated bearer tokens accepted by this process. Unset = no auth (dev only) [env: GD_TOKENS]
      --oidc-issuer <OIDC_ISSUER>
          OpenID Connect issuer URL; enables SSO bearer tokens (JWTs) alongside static tokens [env: GD_OIDC_ISSUER=]
      --oidc-audience <OIDC_AUDIENCE>
          Expected `aud` claim of OIDC tokens [env: GD_OIDC_AUDIENCE=]
      --oidc-claim <OIDC_CLAIM>
          Claim used as the principal for access rules (sub, email, preferred_username...) [env: GD_OIDC_CLAIM=] [default: sub]
      --oidc-require <OIDC_REQUIRE>
          CLAIM=VALUE every OIDC token must carry (repeatable; all must match), e.g. `repository_owner=acme`, `hd=corp.example`, `email_verified=true`. Required for issuers that serve anyone (GitHub Actions, Google) [env: GD_OIDC_REQUIRE=]
      --oidc-admin <OIDC_ADMINS>
          Platform administrators who may sign in through OIDC (repeatable). Any other `--platform-admins` login is refused from an OIDC token, so an identity provider that lets users pick their name can't make someone an administrator [env: GD_OIDC_ADMINS=]
      --tls-cert <TLS_CERT>
          PEM certificate and key for TLS [env: GD_TLS_CERT=]
      --tls-key <TLS_KEY>
          [env: GD_TLS_KEY=]
  -h, --help
          Print help
```

## `grovedockd backup`

```text
Back up a platform server while it runs: a consistent snapshot of the registry and of every hosted repository's metadata database, with a manifest of where each belongs and where objects live. Restore by copying back while stopped (docs/backup.md)

Usage: grovedockd backup [OPTIONS] --platform <PLATFORM> --repos-metadata <REPOS_METADATA> --to <TO>

Options:
      --platform <PLATFORM>
          [env: GD_PLATFORM]
      --repos-metadata <REPOS_METADATA>
          [env: GD_REPOS_METADATA]
      --repos-objects <REPOS_OBJECTS>
          [env: GD_REPOS_OBJECTS] [default: metadata]
      --metadata <METADATA>
          The server's default repository, backed up too when it is SQLite [env: GD_METADATA]
      --to <TO>
          A new or empty directory, or an object store URL (s3://BUCKET/PREFIX, gs://, az://)
      --metrics <METRICS>
          Address for `/metrics` (Prometheus), `/healthz` and `/readyz` (no token needed), e.g. 0.0.0.0:9420 [env: GD_METRICS=]
      --log-json
          Emit JSON logs [env: GD_LOG_JSON=]
      --audit-log <AUDIT_LOG>
          Append an audit trail (JSON lines: who read or changed what, from where, with what result) to this file. Off by default; it grows with every request [env: GD_AUDIT_LOG=]

      --cors-origin <WEB_ORIGINS>
          Origins allowed to call this server from a browser on another site (repeatable or comma-separated), e.g. your own console's address. Default: none (same origin only); `*` allows any (development only) [env: GD_WEB_ORIGINS=] [alias: --web-origins]
      --trust-proxy
          Take the client address (audit log, sign-in rate limits) from `X-Forwarded-For` when the connection comes from a reverse proxy on this host (loopback) [env: GD_TRUST_PROXY=]
      --max-request-mb <MAX_REQUEST_MB>
          Largest request message in MiB (an uploaded object batch, a changeset). Default: 64 with --platform, 260 otherwise. Files of 8 MiB and more are uploaded in chunks [env: GD_MAX_REQUEST_MB=]
      --max-calls-per-principal <MAX_CALLS_PER_PRINCIPAL>
          Calls one account may have in progress at once (0: no limit). Default: 128 with --platform, no limit otherwise [env: GD_MAX_CALLS_PER_PRINCIPAL=]
      --sqlite-synchronous <SQLITE_SYNCHRONOUS>
          SQLite durability: `full` (default) syncs every commit, so an acknowledged land survives power loss; `normal` survives process crashes only, for more throughput on a slow disk [env: GD_SQLITE_SYNCHRONOUS=] [default: full] [possible values: full, normal]
      --allow-anonymous
          Accept unauthenticated calls on a non-loopback address. Without tokens or OIDC, grovedockd otherwise listens only on localhost, so a server is never open to a network by accident [env: GD_ALLOW_ANONYMOUS=]
      --request-timeout <REQUEST_TIMEOUT>
          Longest any one call may run, in seconds [env: GD_REQUEST_TIMEOUT=] [default: 600]
      --max-in-flight <MAX_IN_FLIGHT>
          Calls in progress at once across all clients; beyond this, calls are refused with Unavailable (clients retry) instead of queueing [env: GD_MAX_IN_FLIGHT=] [default: 4096]
      --tokens <TOKENS>
          Comma-separated bearer tokens accepted by this process. Unset = no auth (dev only) [env: GD_TOKENS]
      --oidc-issuer <OIDC_ISSUER>
          OpenID Connect issuer URL; enables SSO bearer tokens (JWTs) alongside static tokens [env: GD_OIDC_ISSUER=]
      --oidc-audience <OIDC_AUDIENCE>
          Expected `aud` claim of OIDC tokens [env: GD_OIDC_AUDIENCE=]
      --oidc-claim <OIDC_CLAIM>
          Claim used as the principal for access rules (sub, email, preferred_username...) [env: GD_OIDC_CLAIM=] [default: sub]
      --oidc-require <OIDC_REQUIRE>
          CLAIM=VALUE every OIDC token must carry (repeatable; all must match), e.g. `repository_owner=acme`, `hd=corp.example`, `email_verified=true`. Required for issuers that serve anyone (GitHub Actions, Google) [env: GD_OIDC_REQUIRE=]
      --oidc-admin <OIDC_ADMINS>
          Platform administrators who may sign in through OIDC (repeatable). Any other `--platform-admins` login is refused from an OIDC token, so an identity provider that lets users pick their name can't make someone an administrator [env: GD_OIDC_ADMINS=]
      --tls-cert <TLS_CERT>

      --tls-key <TLS_KEY>

          Print help
```
